Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate a widened, lobulated anterior mediastinal silhouette (confirmed by the retrosternal opacity on the lateral view) accompanied by bilateral pleural effusions (blunted costophrenic angles), which are findings consistent with an aggressive anterior mediastinal mass such as lymphoma or thymoma with possible vascular/lymphatic involvement. Options A and E are incorrect because the mass is anterior, not posterior; C describes hilar adenopathy rather than a primary mediastinal mass; and D contradicts the presence of effusions which suggest invasion or spread.
